diagnosis.rootCause:
Almost every item in this cluster comes from one problem: builders place a part at a fixed local height or with a random offset and rotation, and never check the part against the ground, the prop's own walls or other props.
(1) Inn(): the hanging sign board sits 0.17 m below its bracket with nothing joining them. It is the wooden slab in oakhaven-02: the inn is right behind the Great Oak camera, and seen close up the board reads as floating.
(2) Broadleaf(): each limb is a cylinder centred at (±.45, h*.92), tilted 35° and then spun about its own middle by a random yaw. Its lower end often points away from the trunk and hangs in mid-air (oakhaven-99).
(3) Tannery(): the scraping beam is tilted 22° about a centre at y .55. The low end floats about 0.1 m up and the high end is in the air with no support (oakhaven-97). Pelts start 0.06 m above the ground. The Maud Tanner overlap looks like occlusion by the second hide frame from the capture angle; her stand is 0.8 m from the rack, so I did not change it.
(4) Oven(): the "woodstack" is a 1×1.8×0.6 grey stone block beside the dome. From the landmark camera it reads as a chimney cutting through the dome. The white spheres are flour sacks that read as eggs. The peel handle's foot sits inside the plinth and its blade floats 0.4 m away from the handle (oakhaven-13).
(5) House(): the door is 2.1 m tall and starts at the plinth top (0.6 m), so it hangs above the ground. Braces every 2.6 m cross the door. The mid rail at .6+wh/2 (2.1 m) runs through the windows (1.9–2.6 m) (oakhaven-12).
(6) crates variant 2: the third crate is at x 1.3, y 1.35, which is past the end of the crate under it, so it sits on nothing. oakhaven.json puts the Harrow-yard lamp (-84,38) between the cart's shafts (oakhaven-07). A second crate prop (-40,46) sits 0.5 m inside the tithe barn's end wall.
(7) RuinedHouse(): four 3–5 m charred beams get random position, yaw, pitch and roll anywhere in the footprint. They poke through the walls, hang over the grass and show as dark wedges in wall faces (khaven-04, ashrim-04, ashrim-06, peaks-04). The roof remnant (Euler 14,8,-22 at y .9) drops a corner about 0.7 m below ground, so it comes out under the plinth (ashrim-06) and cuts through wall tops (khaven-04). GableRoof also left the slab thickness open at both gable ends, so the eave slab reads as a loose board.
(8) Props are seated at the ground height of their centre. The plinth, footing and ruin blocks start at local y 0, so on slopes the downhill side hangs over the ground (peaks-04 waystation slab).
(9) Grove and forest-edge trees have no spacing check (NearProp even skips trees), so two trunks can spawn on top of each other (khaven-06).
(10) A flying crow's wings are 0.04 m wide slivers that flap about the body's long axis, so they are invisible. A crow in flight (for example after the capture teleport scares it off the gibbet) looks like a perched crow hanging in mid-air (peaks-03). Landing and perching already use the ground.

diagnosis.rootCause:
(1) Pale (peaks-06 High Ledge; also the Khaven crypt watcher): Build() gave the Pale a non-uniform Body scale (.82, 1.3, .82) and skipped Features(), so there was no neck or shoulders. The head sphere was re-scaled to (.24, .46, .26) and raised to .9, and the arm pivots got a non-uniform scale under an already non-uniform parent. The result was a stretched egg floating clear above a boxy torso, arms that shear as they swing, and feet sunk 0.3 m into the ground (legs scaled below the pivot). It was flat white with a brown belt, so it read as a broken placeholder. Fix: a dedicated BuildPale() with Body left unscaled and every part at its true height (feet at -1), about 2.4 m tall. It has a floor-length robe (a ZoneMeshes cone from hem to collar, so no gap is possible), a narrow chest, high shoulders, and a tall hood resting on the collar. Its face is a small eyeless gold mask; CANON: the book1 Pale King avatar is 'impossibly tall' with a 'featureless mask of pure gold' and no eyes. It has over-long sleeves with thin pale hands and a faint self-lit pallor. No legs show, so it glides. The watchers themselves stay GAME-ONLY.
(2) Weave-Eater: it went through BuildBeast as a hunched quadruped with long front legs, back spines and a lamprey mouth, which reads as a big dog. CANON (book1 ch.20): these are manifestations of the Wasting from frayed threads of the broken Weave, with no faces and no discernible limbs, 'towering silhouettes'. They drift, move by 'a sudden, jerking displacement of space', and salted ones calcify into white crystal. Fix: a new BuildEater() and a per-frame Drift().
- Build: a dark glossy void core with a lopsided crown, about 2.7 m tall. It has a broken shell of grey static shards (a few emissive violet), 12 frayed threads hanging and 5 whipping off the top. The lowest thread ends about 0.35 m above the ground, so it hovers.
- Motion: the figure is held at a world anchor while the NavMeshAgent root moves on. It snaps to the root every 0.12–0.3 s when moving, 0.6–2.2 s when idle, or whenever the lag passes 0.9 m. Each snap brings a 0.05–0.12 s non-uniform stretch and yaw jerk, shards flickering on and off, a slow bob and a slow roll. There are no legs.
- Death: all renderers swap to a white crystal material and it stands upright as a statue. This overrides EncounterEnemy's tip-over. Respawn restores it.
- Still targetable: the root CapsuleCollider is unchanged, with radius .6 now. IsBeast still includes WeaveEater, so the health multiplier and the agent speed of 3.4 are unchanged. BuildBeast loses its dead Weave-Eater branches.
(3) Other defects seen in the shots:
- (a) Khaven 99-creek/99-wading 'followers clipping and stacked nameplates': this was the capture harness. The lineup parked every non-group trades villager at (-40+i, -40), 1 m apart and left posed (Villager disabled). In Khaven that spot is the creek, so NavMesh warps heaped them on one bank, and they stayed there for all the 99-shots. Oakhaven's 'row of 15 villagers behind a fence' is the same bug. Fix: Villager.Park()/Release(); the lineup hides the others (no body, no nameplate) and puts everyone back to their routine afterwards.
- (b) Crows 'perched in mid-air' (peaks-03): the wings were .04 x .22 planks along the body, rolled about their own long axis, so a flying crow never showed spread wings. Fix: shoulder hinges with .34 m spans, folded back along the body on the ground, beating on take-off and landing and gliding mid-flight.
- (c) Boars and wolves overlapping the player and each other (khaven-99-ambush-sprung): every agent had radius .45 and stoppingDistance 1.8. A 1.9 m-long boar lunging at 8.4 m/s coasts about 2 m past its stop point. Fix: beasts and Weave-Eaters get radius .6 and stoppingDistance 2.1 (reach is still 2.6), and an enemy's velocity is zeroed once it is within stopping distance.
- (d) Hidden ambushers showing as sunk brown humps outside the grass (khaven-99-ambush-before): Hide() sank every body 0.55 m, and camp spawn used a square of ±radius. GrassField only guarantees tall grass inside 30% of the patch (radius+4) on non-open ground. Fix: beasts now lie with belly on the ground and legs folded (LieDepth .21 boar, .39 wolf). Ambushers spawn and respawn within EncounterEnemy.AmbushSpread(radius), about 42% of the radius.
Out of scope, left alone: nameplate offsets and occlusion, the Ashrim salt-trader standing beside his stall (stall navmesh/stand point), and landmark camera framing.

No error is raised. Fix: GetComponentsInChildren<Renderer>(true).

The robe cone (base .42, apex 1.33) is wider than the arms below hip height. The cuffs were about half inside the cone, and the 'long, thin hands' (body-local y -0.18 to -0.42, x about 0.18–0.28, where the cone is about 0.29 wide) were entirely inside it. The hand centre is now at x about 0.355, against a robe radius of 0.268. The walk swing still works.

Fix: a speed test, sqrMagnitude > .25*dt*dt (faster than 0.5 m/s), which holds at any frame rate.

Minor: Park() did not hide the hen-wife's egg basket. The basket is not in Villager.renderers, because it is collected while inactive, so a parked, carrying hen-wife would leave a basket floating where she stood. Fix: SetActive(false) on the basket, as Villager.Hide() already does.

diagnosis.rootCause:
These are six separate defects, all confirmed from the screenshots, the builder code and the zone data.

1. oakhaven-05, The Wasting: the landmark sits at (50,0), in the village meadow. The zone's Wasting starts at x=84 (fade 20) and ends at x=104, where the curtain stands. So the generic south-west shot showed ordinary grass. Fix: move the landmark to (96,2) and give it an authored view looking due east at the grey band and curtain.

2. oakhaven-03, The Golden Cask: the inn is at rotation 221, so its door, sign, lantern and barrels face north-east toward the green. The capture tour always frames a landmark from its south-west (`EncounterCapture` uses `from = at + (-.6,-.8)*dist`), which lands on the windowed back wall. Fix: an authored view from the green side.
   - The stand point is (-5,-10) with pitch 19 and zoom 13.
   - The camera ends up about 6 m from the Great Oak. The oak has TreeFade, so the camera does not collide with it.
   - At this pitch the player's head sits below the door threshold, and the sign sits above the head.

3. oakhaven-09, Old wayshrine: it was a `ruin` prop, five random stone boxes, with a boulder beside it. Fix: a new `shrine` prop kind.
   - The shape: stone steps and a pillar carrying a small gabled niche, with a pale figure inside and a sun-disc on the gable. At its foot are a bowl, two lit candle stubs and offerings in `art.ash` grey ("turned grey and brittle").
   - It now faces west, and is framed from the west with the Wasting behind it.
   - The offerings deliberately use 15 `R01` draws, the same number the old `Ruin(5)` used. This keeps Oakhaven's random stream, so every later prop, grove and forest-edge tree stays exactly where it was.

4. khaven-09, Drowned graveyard: there was no water there at all. Fix: add a real `ZoneLake` called "Drowned graves", centre (4,-99), radius 5.5, depth 0.85.
   - The depth has to be at least 0.8: `ZoneWater` forces lake depth to max(.8, depth), and WaterTests fails the centre-depth check if the difference is over 0.1.
   - At 0.85 it is wading depth, well under the 1.35 m swim threshold.
   - Because it is part of the water model, drawn, carved and felt water agree. It gets Khaven's dark Gloom tint, muddy shore paint, and no grass inside the shoreline.
   - I worked out the pond's wobble from its `System.Random` seed (135451) and placed four graves in the shallows at 0.3-0.6 m deep, one on the bank, and one upright.
   - Grave `variant` 1 now means heaved over (14-22 degrees) and half sunk. It uses the same two random draws per grave, so the stream is unchanged. All graves also sink 4 cm so no edge floats.
   - The landmark point moves to the pool centre. The shot is taken from the east (17,-97), outside the Hollow Men camp's radius, with the ruined chapel wall at the left of the frame.

5. khaven-04, The Cracked Hearth: the camera was wedged between the town wall and the ruined smithy, looking at blank walls, and nothing on the inn read as a "cracked hearth". On the canon map the Cracked Hearth is the intact inn with a smoking chimney, and villagers drink there. So I did not build it as a ruin, which would contradict canon and remove Khaven's inn. Instead, inn `variant` 1 (only the Cracked Hearth uses it) gets `CrackedHearth()`:
   - a sooty stone chimney breast on the hearth gable, lined up with the hearth inside;
   - a glowing zig-zag crack running up it from a glowing ash-pit door, with the fire showing through ("the fire has not gone out");
   - the stack above leans off a glowing seam, and there are fallen stones at its foot.

   It uses no random draws. The Golden Cask (variant 0) keeps its roof stack; an outside breast there would clip its hedge. The authored view is from the east, stand point (0,13), pitch 12, zoom 13. It shows both the door front and the cracked gable, and the chimney top fits in the frame. I checked the camera line against the Fallen Smithy, the crates and the Hovel footprints: it clears all three.

6. khaven-10, Creek barrow: the generic stand point put the camera about y=-118, inside the south forest-edge tree line, which runs from y=-115 to -118. The barrow was also a stone hut, not a barrow. Fix: crypt `variant` 1 builds a turf mound.
   - The mound is a large sunk ellipsoid, so it sits on sloping ground.
   - It has two stone jambs and a lintel around a black doorway, the sealing slab thrown down in front, and nine kerb stones set on the real ground height.
   - The six random headstones keep their 30 draws, and now also follow the ground.
   - The view is from the north-north-east (48,-90). That is outside the Grey Sexton's camp radius and clear of trees, looking at the entrance about 40 degrees off-axis.

**Supporting change.** `ZoneLabel` gets optional `view` (a Vector2 stand point), `viewPitch` and `viewZoom`. The tour uses them when set; otherwise it keeps the generic south-west framing. I also updated the docs and lore labels: the wayshrine is GAME-ONLY, the cracked chimney is marked as a GAME-ONLY reading of the canon name, and the flood pool and barrow mound are GAME-ONLY.

review.notes:
The proposal is sound apart from two landmark shots that cut off their own subject, the Cracked Hearth chimney and the Golden Cask roof. I corrected those two views and widened the crack. All other edits are carried over unchanged. I checked framing with a projection script at the scene camera's 55 degree vertical FOV; nothing was rendered.

What I checked:
- **oldStrings:** every one exists exactly once in the current files, and no two edits overlap. All target files use CRLF line endings. The multi-line oldStrings are written with LF, so they only match if the patch tool normalises line endings (Claude Code's Edit tool does).
- **Compiles:**
  - `Crypt(t, p.variant)` has a default parameter.
  - The local function `Foot` captures `t` and calls the instance `HeightAt`.
  - The braced `grave` case declares `a` and `b` with no clash in the switch.
  - Loop variables such as `s` and `i` are declared in sibling scopes only.
  - `GableRoof` has a 4-argument overload, and `art.ash`, `art.glass` and `art.foliage` exist.
  - `CrackedHearth` receives `w`, `H` and `roofH` from `Inn`.
  - The capture tuple takes floats. No name clashes with `Shrine`, `CrackedHearth` or `Foot`.
  - JSON: `JsonUtility` reads the new `view`, `viewPitch` and `viewZoom` fields, and a missing field gives zero, so the default framing is kept.
- **Random stream:**
  - The shrine takes 15 draws, the same as `Ruin(5)`.
  - Crypt headstones keep their 30 draws in the same order.
  - The graves keep 2 draws each, in the same order.
  - The shrine's `NearProp` radius falls from 7.5 to 5, but no Oakhaven grove is within 30 m of it.
  - The Khaven pond is more than 20 m from every grove and from the forest-edge `NearWater` band.
- **WaterTests:**
  - The lake edge-float check passes by construction: the level is 0.05 below the lowest natural ground in a ring out to 3 m, so the drawn edge is at least 0.024 above the level.
  - The centre depth is exactly 0.85, unless the natural centre happens to be a pit more than 0.85 m below that ring (unlikely).
  - Crows are exempt, and WorldLife crows avoid water anyway.
  - I reproduced the grave depths from `System.Random` seed 135451: 0.43, 0.58, 0.37 and 0.29 m. The bank grave is 0.88 m out; the upright one is 2.7 m out.
- **ZoneContentTests:** the pond is wading depth (swimInset 0), so it is navmesh area 3 and walkable, and the Gloom Creek hollows still spawn. No quest visit point or interactable is affected. Villagers can wade.
- **Lore:** the canon map draws the Cracked Hearth as the intact inn with a chimney, so the proposal is right not to build it as a ruin.

Remaining risks, not fixed:
- The Wasting and wayshrine views stand on Oakhaven's 5 m hills, and the graveyard and barrow views on Khaven's 2.6 m hills. If the ground rises behind the player, the camera's sphere cast will pull it in. Re-shoot and adjust the view numbers in JSON if so.
- The barrow's stone doorway stands in front of the mound's upper slope. From the 42 degree view you see turf behind the lintel, not sky, so it reads as a doorway in front of the mound. That is acceptable.
- The grave height change also lowers the other graves 4 cm. Headstones now follow the ground at the Old Crypt and at Ashrim's Ash-Walker caves (both variant 0), a small intended improvement.
- If another agent edits the landmark loop in EncounterCapture, keep the `l.view` override when merging.

diagnosis.rootCause:
The world tour's landmark and exit shots use the player's orbit camera. EncounterCapture teleports the player to a fixed point south-west of the landmark (from = at + (-.6,-.8)*min(r+4,14)) and calls SetView(yaw,17,11). That spot is never checked against anything. AdventurerMotor.LateUpdate then sphere-casts from the player's head back toward the camera and pulls the camera in to the first scenery hit, with a minimum of 1.2 m. That hit can be a farmhouse wall, a cliff box or a ruin wall. The camera ends up on the back of the player's head (oakhaven-10, peaks-06/08, khaven-08, ashrim-08) or pinned against walls (khaven-04). Tree colliders are skipped, so in woods the camera sits inside trunks and crowns (khaven-05/10, oakhaven-18). Even when nothing blocks, the orbit camera always centres the player, and the player hides the landmark. The fixed 11 m distance ignores the landmark's size, so tall ones like the Great Oak are cut off at the top. The fixed south-west bearing also ignores which way a building faces, so the Golden Cask and Cracked Hearth are shot from their blank back walls.

The fix gives landmark and exit shots a searched free-camera viewpoint in EncounterCapture:
- **Sizing:** the landmark is sized from the prop that carries its name (its renderers' bounds, so the shot centres on the real object), or else from the scenery colliders and tree crowns inside its circle.
- **Search:** 16 bearings × 3 distances. Distance is sized so the footprint fills about three quarters of the frame width and the height fits in frame; the camera height is lower for tall landmarks. Buildings start from their door side (-Z, turned 25°), everything else from the south-west.
- **Rejected spots:** outside the zone, inside scenery or within 0.5 m of a tree crown, a sight line to the landmark's middle that dips under water, or one blocked by solid scenery before it reaches the landmark's circle.
- **Scoring:** penalties for turning away from the preferred side, for changing distance, for each tree in the sight line, for a hidden base and for a roof under the camera.

For the shot, the motor is disabled, the camera is placed directly looking at the landmark, and the player is hidden 2 m behind the camera. TreeFade.UpdateAll is called each frame with an end point that stops short of the landmark's own trees, so trees in the way fade but the Great Oak or the Whispering Wood never fade. If no spot passes, the shot falls back to the exact old orbit framing and logs a line. Shot names and order are unchanged.
